clue.text: Not a happy bunny?

parts.note: the idiom for someone displeased, taken literally of a rabbit that is furious and bouncing about

explanation.surface: A sympathetic remark about someone who is clearly fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a happy bunny' is a British idiom for someone annoyed; the answer is a furious person, and a bunny is a creature that hops.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone furious is certainly displeased, and the hopping half of the idiom suits a rabbit.

clue.text: Small problem affected church

parts.note: to affect someone badly is to hit them

explanation.surface: A minor difficulty has had an impact on a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a minor snag or temporary obstacle.

clue.text: Forecast is for good numbers at first

indicators.note: the other pieces come first, with the word is following them at the end

parts.note: to be for something is to be pro it

explanation.surface: A forecast predicting good figures in the early stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' looks like it describes the numbers, but it places the other pieces ahead of 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a forecast, especially of how an illness will develop.

clue.text: An asteroid is what we didn't expect to meet here?

definitions.text: An asteroid is what we didn't expect to meet here?

parts.words: An asteroid is what we didn't expect to meet here?
parts.note: the stock remark on an unexpected encounter, taken literally: an asteroid is a tiny planet-like body

explanation.surface: Astronauts surprised to bump into someone on an asteroid.
explanation.walkthrough: People say the phrase when they meet someone unexpectedly; read literally, an asteroid is indeed a little world.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom greets a chance meeting, and an asteroid is literally a minor planet.

clue.text: Gang's leaders were furious to be put away

parts.note: the leading two letters of the word gang
raged means were furious

explanation.surface: The heads of a gang were angry at being locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' is plural, so take the first two letters of Gang. 'put away' is the definition, used of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that is put away for the night is stored in its garage.

clue.text: Judge a head on real ale sound

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of real
signals that a word for ale is said aloud and spelt like a near match

parts.note: bitter is a type of British ale

explanation.surface: Someone deciding whether a real ale is in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a classic British draught beer; spoken, it gives the ending BITER.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone who settles disputes or decides, like a judge.

clue.text: Gestured with contempt in quarrel

definitions.meaning: expelled saliva as a show of disdain

explanation.surface: Someone showed scorn during an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of spit, and a small row or squabble.

clue.text: Saucy work from poets translated

indicators.note: translating changes one form into another, so the letters of poets are rearranged

explanation.surface: A risqué piece of writing rendered from verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' suggests cheeky, but here it means made into a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is a sauce produced by pounding basil, pine nuts and cheese.

clue.text: Cause to get agitated in warm air, as body in part lost fluid on track

definitions.text: Cause to get agitated in warm air

parts.note: the tum is the stomach, one part of the body
bled means lost blood
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A strange account of an injured runner bleeding on a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry machines with heated drums toss clothes about in warm air to dry them.

clue.text: Passes inspection team but is ignored

parts.note: goes by means passes
the board is the panel that inspects or examines

explanation.surface: Something clears the inspectors yet still gets overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something being discarded or neglected, like an item tossed overboard.

clue.text: For oneself, take time by alarm-clock

parts.note: an alarm clock is something that rouses you, a rouser

explanation.surface: Instructions about setting an alarm clock for your own use.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb the answer means pocket, to take money for yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to pocket something, particularly money, is to keep it in one's own possession.

clue.text: Wanting to flourish, fail endlessly, admitting defeat

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so one piece goes inside the other
the final letter of the word for fail is cut off

parts.note: to bomb is to fail badly
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: Someone eager to succeed keeps failing and concedes defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the word for fail, and 'admitting' takes the defeat inside it; 'Wanting to' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to develop and thrive, just as plants put forth flowers.

clue.text: Daughter's relieved expression, cracking clue —— easy with this?

indicators.note: cracking a word open lets other letters inside it

parts.note: a hint is a clue
D is the abbreviation for daughter
a sigh is a sound expressing relief

explanation.surface: A daughter sighs with relief after solving a clue, adding that it was easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition draws on the saying that everything is easy looking back.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially, decisions seem simple after the event, when we know how things turned out.

clue.text: Having dredged-up material, turn over empty borders

indicators.note: having means containing, so one piece holds the other
the word for borders is turned to read backwards

parts.note: lips are edges or borders
O, zero, signifies nothing, emptiness

explanation.surface: Someone brings up silt and then flips over the blank margins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn over' makes SPIL from LIPS, and 'Having' holds the O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoil is the waste earth and silt dug out during excavation or dredging.

clue.text: Crush a high-ranking officer

parts.note: a pash is a schoolgirl's crush or infatuation

explanation.surface: Someone has a crush on a senior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Ottoman Empire this title went to senior military commanders and governors.

clue.text: Writer is inquisitive, yet fails to pen a line

parts.note: someone who pries is being nosy

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so one piece goes inside
the word yet breaks down, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nosy author who never manages to write anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails' rearranges YET to TEY, and 'to pen' puts L inside it to make TLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: J B Priestley was an English novelist and playwright, author of An Inspector Calls.

clue.text: Right to interrupt homework with message, one that's unpopular

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into something, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement work
a word is a message, as in sending word

explanation.surface: Breaking into someone's homework with a message is resented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homework' is DIY, British do-it-yourself home repairs, not school work.
explanation.definitionFit: A term regarded as shameful or disliked is described as being taboo, out of favour.

clue.text: Convenient to be up pronto, moving with energy

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifted around into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: It's handy to get up quickly and get going energetically.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timely and well suited to the occasion is convenient.

clue.text: Protected from being treated rudely about article

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: insulted means treated rudely
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Shielded from rude treatment concerning a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulated means shielded or protected from outside influences, as wiring is.

clue.text: Turn up but stand round a bit more

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word but from bottom to top

parts.note: a bier is a stand for a coffin

explanation.surface: Someone arrives but stands around for a little longer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubby means plump or rotund, so its comparative is slightly more rotund.

clue.text: Party almost unattractive to a small boy

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the word for unattractive is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: ugly means unattractive

explanation.surface: A party that was nearly ugly for a little lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas is a male first name, so an example of a boy.

clue.text: Record having a roll in the grass? Maybe once

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the dried grass

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: rolling over turns the record's letters backwards

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A record of a romp in the hay, perhaps from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: A roll in the hay is slang for sex; here 'having a roll' turns the record round before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Haply is an archaic word for perhaps, so it meant maybe in former times.

clue.text: A number of shots succeeded at Oval ground

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

indicators.note: ground is the past participle of grind, so the letters are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A batsman's volley of strokes paid off at the Oval cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground; 'ground' looks like part of its name but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of several guns.

clue.text: Immature creature hides right inside rock

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: lava is molten or solidified volcanic rock

explanation.surface: A young animal is concealed within a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young, wingless stage of an insect before it matures.

clue.text: Cried like a whale

definitions.meaning: covered in the thick fat of whales

explanation.surface: Someone sobbed hugely.
explanation.definitionFit: It means wept noisily, and also padded with the thick fat that whales carry.

clue.text: Manage to sleep soundly? They never got up

parts.note: to do is to manage, as in we can do

indicators.note: signals that the word for sleep is said aloud

parts.note: to doze is to sleep lightly

explanation.surface: Advice on getting a good night's rest, then remarks on lie-ins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like part of sound sleep but signals a word spoken aloud. The definition plays on flightless birds never getting airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: These extinct birds of Mauritius were flightless, so they never rose into the air.

clue.text: Mythical figure telling a lot of Liverpudlian's story

indicators.note: telling means saying out loud, so the phrase is pronounced

parts.note: a Liverpudlian says lorra for lot of, as Cilla Black's catchphrase 'a lorra lorra laughs'; a story is a lie

explanation.surface: A Scouser recounting a long tale about a legendary being.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpudlians are mocked for saying 'lorra' for 'lot of', as Cilla Black, a Liverpool entertainer, did; a lie is a story, giving LORRA LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend she was a siren on a Rhine rock whose singing lured boatmen to ruin.

clue.text: Suppressing fever, conducted in concert

indicators.note: suppressing something holds it down within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: led means conducted or guided
ague is a malarial fever

explanation.surface: A conductor led a concert despite being feverish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conducted' and 'concert' suggest music, but 'in concert' means acting together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allied or united is acting together, jointly, as one body.

clue.text: Informal agreement: you sound surprised

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone casually agrees but sounds taken aback.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a casual, colloquial form of yes.

clue.text: Go over to sort of rehearsal and act the part of Viola?

parts.note: to cross is to go over
a dress rehearsal is a final run-through in costume

explanation.surface: An actor heads to the dress rehearsal to play Viola.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, Viola disguises herself as a young man, Cesario.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola wears men's clothing for most of the play, so playing her means wearing the opposite sex's clothes.
